dish.title: Korean Maeuntang: Spicy Cod Stew with Radish, Tofu, and Watercress
dish.description: Chunks of cod simmered in a fiery broth of gochugaru, gochujang, garlic, soy sauce, and fish sauce with Korean radish, onion, zucchini, and tofu, finished with watercress, scallions, and sliced jalapeno and served with short-grain rice.

recipe_version.title: Korean Maeuntang: Spicy Cod Stew with Radish, Tofu, and Watercress
recipe_version.description: Chunks of cod simmered in a fiery broth of gochugaru, gochujang, garlic, soy sauce, and fish sauce with Korean radish, onion, zucchini, and tofu, finished with watercress, scallions, and sliced jalapeno and served with short-grain rice.

ingredients.name: gochujang
ingredients.display_name: gochujang whose label lists rice, chile, soybeans, wheat, and salt

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.display_name: fish sauce whose label lists anchovy and salt (sugar allowed), no shrimp

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Peel and cut the radish, slice the onion and zucchini, mince the garlic, cut the tofu and cod, cut the scallions, slice the jalapeno, and rinse the rice until the rinse runs clear.

steps.title: Season the broth
steps.body: Stir the garlic, gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, fish sauce, and salt into 6 cups water in the 5.5-quart Dutch oven.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: While the stew cooks (overlap stated): combine the rice and 1 3/4 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, then cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat to rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the radish
steps.body: Add the radish and onion to the broth, cover, and bring to a boil over high, about 10 minutes to come to a boil. Simmer until the radish turns translucent, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Poach the fish
steps.body: Add the zucchini and tofu and simmer 3 minutes. Slide in the cod and simmer gently, without stirring, until it flakes and reads 145 F, about 6 minutes. Lay the watercress, scallions, and jalapeno on top for the last minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Ladle into bowls with the rice alongside.

coverage_contribution: Korean fish in the catalog is a braised mackerel with radish; there is no spicy fish soup-stew (jjigae or tang) with fish. An easy, HH001-eligible fish dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with korean-braised-mackerel-radish: a brothy chile stew of cod, tofu, and greens eaten with a spoon, not mackerel braised down in a thick soy-chile glaze. Compared with korean-soft-tofu-stew: cod and radish in a clear red broth, not silken tofu and egg in a thick stew. Compared with filipino-fish-sinigang: chile-hot rather than tamarind-sour.
not_duplicate_of: Not budae jjigae (no meat or noodles) and not haemul jeongol (no shellfish).
